docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Each entry is a symptom, what causes it, and what to do. ~/TandemLLM/bin/tandem logs follows the server log on an installed engine, and GET /v1/dashboard/logs streams it. TandemApp's docs has the dashboard's, the Chat tab's and the proxy's entries.

docs.title: Installing
docs.text:
The installer stops: no tag, branch or commit 'v0.16.0'. The repository it clones has no such tag. The installer clones the repository --repo names, the public one by default, at the tag --ref names, v0.16.0 by default. To install from another repository, such as a fork, pass its address with --repo. The same missing tag makes curl answer 404 for the installer's own URL.

install.sh -{}-setup refuses: the directory already has a configured engine. A box that switched to a profile counts as configured, and --setup would stop that engine. To update it, add --force-setup, then run use-profile.sh with the profile again; its files are already on disk.

use-profile.sh refuses the download: not enough disk. The fetcher keeps 60 GB free after every download, per filesystem, and counts the profile's weights and the files beside them first. --dry-run prints each file with its size. Free the space, or pick a smaller profile: exl3-2.5 needs 12.0 GB of weights beside the 27B's shared 40 GB.

A download stopped halfway. Run the same use-profile.sh command again. It keeps every file that finished and checked, pins the same commit, and continues; a folder appears only when all its files are there.

The setup guide's community section says “no published list yet”. GitHub answered 404 for models/community-index.json on the public repository's main: no release there carries the list yet. That is a note, not an error. The page shows the list from the box's last fetch, or the one that came with its release, and Refresh asks again (Where the list comes from). A real failure shows one short line instead, such as “GitHub could not be reached”, and the server's log has the URL.

docs.title: The engine
docs.text:
The start refuses: an engine is already alive. One engine per board. Two engines loading side by side run a DGX Spark out of memory, and a board in that state stops answering until a power cycle. A loading engine counts although it answers nothing yet, because it binds its port only after the weights are in. . ops/engines.sh; engine_pids lists every engine process; stop the other one before starting. The same rule holds for a vLLM or SGLang on the same board: check the free memory first and keep at least 15 GiB of MemAvailable at the worst case.

A request gets a 503 with Retry-After, and the log names the peak. The memory gate (The memory gate). Before every prefill the engine gives memory back cheapest first until the prompt's workspace fits under the declared peak (77 GiB); when it still does not fit, it refuses rather than wedge the board. The System view's memory plan shows what holds memory: a small model beside the engine holds its claim, and a 262,144-token context holds about 13 GiB more than a 131,072-token one. If the refusals go on after a role loaded, unload it in the Conductor view or lower QWEN38_SHADOW_GB.

A role does not load. The residency planner refused it: refused_memory, refused_hold or refused_load_in_progress. It loads one model at a time, never during a hold, and only when the board keeps its floor and margin (15 + 6 GiB) after the engine's growth to its peak and the role's claim. The Deciders screen and the System view say why, and residency.jsonl in the conductor's directory journals each decision. The narrator's keeper tries again in the next idle window.

The engine does not start: the image processor resolved to the pil backend. torchvision is missing or too old. Install the pair that matches torch (pillow==11.3.0, torchvision==0.28.0+cu130 from the CUDA 13.0 index), or start with --image-backend pil, or --vision off for text only. The installer's venv has both.

A benchmark is slower than the paper, or its text differs. With the conductor on, every request runs through the router: a class, an effort cap and a hidden note. Send X-Tandem: raw, or the profile bench, for the raw path. Then check the lookup corpus: the installer builds a public one, and the paper's corpus is not published. And check the store view: a store that has seen the benchmark's prompts inflates it (Measurement).

A client asks for a model name the engine does not list. With the conductor on, /v1/models lists TandemLLM alone, and any model name is served as TandemLLM. Nothing to fix.

A turn waits a long time before its first token. With one sequence (QSE_PARALLEL=1; the shipped profile runs 8 lanes) the engine serves one turn at a time. A streamed request behind a running turn gets an SSE comment every 10 s with its position and an estimate, and with the progress lines on a waiting line in the client; it waits as long as a request may run. A request without a stream gets a 429 after --queue-timeout. Short requests go through the side lane. A full queue (8) is a 503 at once.

A turn waits for memory. The chat or the client says it waits for memory, the response has X-Tandem-Wait: memory, or the Lanes view shows waiting_memory. The turn is paused and starts by itself once memory frees (Waiting for memory). Its line in the dashboard says what it needs, what holds the rest and when the wait ends; the engine log repeats it every 15 s. A streamed turn gives up only after QSE_MEM_WAIT_S (3 hours) with a 503 memory_wait_timeout; one without a stream after --queue-timeout, unless it sends wait_for_memory: true. A shorter conversation or fewer chats at once needs less memory, and a high priority lets the chat that matters go first. Since 0.15.4 a short turn on a long chat is charged the rows it forwards, so a wait of minutes for such a turn is worth a report with the exported log (GET /v1/dashboard/logs/export).

The next turn re-reads the whole conversation. Look at the request's cache source in the Performance view or the Dev view's detail: end, resident, prefix, session, disk, spill, continuation, or none for a cold prefill. A client that rewrites its history (another system text, a changed earlier message) parts from the cached rows where it changed. A short conversation started while a longer one is resident is a guest of it and re-reads its first answer at its second turn. Caches lists each case. With --parallel N, each slot keeps the conversation it served last, and a turn goes back to the slot that holds its conversation (the request row's slot, the [parallel] log line). When memory ran short, the KV pool may have given that conversation's rows back: with the session spill on it wrote them to the NVMe drive (the SSD) first, and the turn reads them back with the cache source spill (Live conversations on the NVMe). With the spill off it reads its prompt again. A new user message in Open WebUI after the agent changed directory used to part at the tool block (its working directory is in run_command's description); under a conductor plan it no longer does (QWEN38_CLIENT_CWD). If the turn's source is none right after short requests of TandemLLM's own (json rows of the router), check refused_stash in /health's resident report and cache.memory against the ceiling.

An agent turn ends with no answer and no tool call. The model wrote its tool call inside its thinking and stopped there. With the session monitor acting and E1 on in the request's profile (a profile stored before this release may have it off: set it to act on the Monitor screen), the call goes out as the answer when it parses and names an offered tool, under the line tool call written in the thinking, sending it; otherwise the turn is continued, and after two tries it ends with one sentence. On the raw path the engine returns what the model wrote.

A long conversation shows X-Tandem-Images-Left-Out. A request carries at most 16 images and 65,536 image rows. When the excess is in earlier messages, the oldest images are left out in steps of 8 and the request is served; only the newest message's own images over a cap are a 400.

The dashboard says the engine is stopped for maintenance or starting. The engine is away and the reverse proxy shows the status responder's page (While the engine is away): the reason, since when, about how long. It opens the dashboard by itself when /health answers.

A request answers 400 and param names a field. The request's shape is wrong: no user message, an unknown role, a late system message, max_tokens below 1, an empty prompt (What the API supports).

Open WebUI shows a literal </think> while an answer streams. Open WebUI 0.11.3 shows the stream piece that carries </think> as message text until the round ends. Under a conductor plan the engine sends Open WebUI its reasoning in reasoning_content, which has no tag; a request with reasoning_format: tags, the raw path, or QWEN38_CLIENT_REASONING set empty bring the tags back. The saved chat is clean either way.

The model writes “Laya unavailable”. Its scripts could not reach the engine from where they run. Set QWEN38_TANDEM_URL to an address that machine reaches.

docs.title: Memory notes
docs.text:
The model never writes a note. Every shipped profile has memory: off; set it to shadow or on. The background writer has its own switch, settings.memory.notes.writer.mode. The log says why a due session was not written: hold, gpu, nothing, moved or no session.

Behind the proxy the writer never runs on a cloud model.

auto is off on a paid cloud model. Switch it on for that backend, give the model a price, and check the day's caps on the backend's page.

A note was refused. Caps refuse, never cut; a body that is mostly a secret is refused; a rule about the user needs the user's own message in the turn. The Notes tab lists the refusals with their reasons.

docs.title: Reference: commands
docs.text: tools/gen_reference.py builds the reference tables from the code: it parses the argument parsers, the settings registry, the metric registrations and the ledger's schema with Python's ast module and never imports the project. tests/test_docs_reference.py runs it with --check, so a table that no longer matches the code fails the tests. A description is the first sentence of the flag's own help text; where the code gives none, the generator carries a short one. A default is the code's; where the served profile passes another value, the cell says “served:” and that value, as ops/start.sh builds it from ops/serve.env.

docs.title: The engine's server
docs.text: python server/app.py [flags], or ops/start.sh, which builds the flags from serve.env. python server/app.py --help prints the full help texts.

docs.title: Every flag of the engine's server, server/app.py, with the value the served profile passes where it differs
docs.text: Flag Default What it does --model none the checkpoint directory of the target model. --served-model qwen3.8-27b-spark-engine; served: qwen38-spark-engine the raw engine's model name; with the conductor on it is a hidden alias of TandemLLM. --host 127.0.0.1; served: 0.0.0.0 the address to bind. --port 8000 the port to listen on. --max-len 8192; served: 262144 context length. The KV buffer is allocated for all of it up front, so this is a memory decision as much as a capability one: 64 KiB a token of engine KV plus 20 KiB a token per drafter arm, 27.9 GB of KV and 53.4 GB of whole ... --rep-penalty 1 deterministic repetition penalty on the target's logits, before the argmax (1.0 = off, today's output). --presence-penalty 0 flat subtraction from tokens already in the history (0 = off). --frequency-penalty 0 subtraction per occurrence, on tokens already in the history (0 = off). --temperature 0 server default sampling temperature (0 = greedy, the exact path). --top-p none server default for top_p. --top-k none server default for top_k (0 is off). --no-repeat-ngram 0 forbid the token that would complete an n-gram already seen (HF's no_repeat_ngram_size; 0 = off, must be >= 2). --pattern-stop none end a generation that repeats one short pattern forever, as MAX:MIN:COUNT (e.g. 64:1:8, a block of 1..64 tokens repeated 8 times ends the generation with finish_reason stop). --argloop on the tool-argument loop guard (server/api/argloop.py): on stops a held tool call whose arguments loop and tells the model on its next turn. One of: on, log, off. --default-max-tokens 8192; served: 32768 what a request that does not send max_tokens gets. --reasoning-format tags how the reasoning block reaches the client: inside <think></think> in content (default, and what Open WebUI folds on), as OpenAI-style reasoning_content deltas, or both. One of: tags, reasoning_content, both. --drafter mtp the drafter set. lenrouter, the served one, holds both DFlash2 widths beside the lookup drafter; none decodes one token a step. One of: mtp, router, merged, dflash2, lenrouter, none. --tree off (a switch) verify a draft TREE per step instead of a chain, where the drafter builds one; see docs/speculative-decoding.md. --regenerate sample (QWEN38_REGENERATE) : a regenerate (the same conversation again after it was answered, under a TandemLLM plan; or X-Tandem-Regenerate: 1) samples with a fresh seed; every other request keeps its own sampling (greedy by default). One of: sample, off. --regenerate-temperature 0.7 (QWEN38_REGEN_TEMPERATURE) a regenerate's temperature (QWEN38_REGEN_TEMPERATURE). --regenerate-top-p 0.95 (QWEN38_REGEN_TOP_P) a regenerate's top-p (QWEN38_REGEN_TOP_P). --regenerate-top-k 20 (QWEN38_REGEN_TOP_K) a regenerate's top-k (QWEN38_REGEN_TOP_K). --sampled-tree none; served: det let a SAMPLED request keep the tree verify. One of: det, mixed. --budget 16 nodes per tree, anchor included. --df2-temp 1 the block drafter's temperature for its own proposals. --corpus none (QWEN38_CORPUS) the lookup drafter's corpus: a directory of token ids with a suffix array (tools/build_corpus.py). --depth 3 the drafter's depth for the older chain drafters. --k 0 verify block size; 0 = the drafter's depth. --draft-head none an optional separate head file for the drafter. --nvfp4 none the NVFP4 weight files to load, one per target (mlp, gdn, attn); empty means the checkpoint's FP8. --price-table none (QSE_PRICE_TABLE) FILE[:NAME], the routers' verify/draft/rollback prices for this weight set (engine/prices.py); empty = the NVFP4 constants in the code. --fp8-head none e4m3 lm_head from tools/quant_head.py; halves the head's 2.54 GB in both the verify pass and the block drafter's top-k read. --dflash2-blocks 1 chained 8-wide draft blocks; 1 proposes 7 tokens, 2 proposes 14. --dflash2-path greedy how the block drafter walks its lattice: the greedy path or Viterbi. One of: greedy, viterbi. --dflash2-ckpt none the narrow (block 8) DFlash2 drafter checkpoint. --dflash2-ckpt16 none the sixteen-wide drafter, for --drafter lenrouter. --len-fixed 0 pin --drafter lenrouter to one block width (8 or 16). 0 lets the policy choose, which means --len-latch: one decision a request. 8 and 16 measure the fixed baselines through the same code. --len-latch on (--no-len-latch turns it off) decide the block width ONCE a request, four wide blocks, up to four narrow probes, then no more switching. --learn-cost on (--no-learn-cost turns it off) the length router learns its verify and draft costs from the blocks it times, across requests (default). --no-learn-cost keeps the served price table; timings inside a request still size its blocks, so two runs can part at a near tie. --len-explore 32 blocks between forced wide probes when nothing suggests one. --deep 0 (QWEN38_DEEP) with --drafter lenrouter --tree: after --deep-after wide blocks in a row commit their whole width, propose the lookup drafter's long exact continuation of this request's text as one chain of up to this many rows. 0 = off. --deep-after 2 (QWEN38_DEEP_AFTER) full wide blocks in a row before a deep chain (2 keeps it off new text). --narrow-arm on with --drafter lenrouter: build the block-8 drafter arm (on, the served default) or run the block-16 arm alone. One of: on, off. --drop-idle off (--drop-idle turns it on); served: on release the arm that LOSES the latch for the rest of the request: no tap, no sync, and nothing of it in the state snapshot. --relax-tau 1 Breaks the agreement rule: accept a drafted token whose probability is at least this fraction of the argmax's. 1.0, the default, keeps the rule. --relax-rank 1 Breaks the agreement rule: accept a drafted token among the target's top r. 1, the default, keeps the rule. --think-stall on with --conductor shadow or on, run the reasoning-loop arms of the policy's reasoning_loop task (a pattern repeated over 128+ tokens, the history-wide 16-gram repeat, novelty collapse); the monitor decides whether a hit closes the ... --no-think-stall sets think_stall off never run the reasoning-loop arms (the budget still applies). --conductor raw the second-level harness (TandemApp's tandemapp/conductor/monitor/). raw, the default (off is the same): nothing of it runs and the output is the raw engine's. shadow: every rule runs and journals, nothing is done. on: each task ... One of: raw, off, shadow, on. --conductor-policy none the monitor's policy file (default TandemApp's ops/supervisor.yaml), validated at start against TandemApp's ops/supervisor.schema.json. --conductor-watch-s 30 with --conductor shadow or on, how often the stall watchdog's watch looks for sessions whose client has gone. --think-budget 0 default cap on reasoning tokens per request, 0 = uncapped. --answer-reserve auto (QSE_ANSWER_RESERVE) tokens of the output limit kept for the answer when a client asks for a thinking budget in any shape (server/api/thinking.py): its reasoning closes early enough to leave them. auto = min(2048, a quarter of the limit), 0 = none ... --reasoning-effort none; served: medium default reasoning_effort for the chat template. One of: none, off, low, medium, xhigh. --cache-budget-gb 2 RAM budget for the state cache, in GiB (CACHE_GB). --store-entry-gb 1 GiB one state-store snapshot may take (STORE_ENTRY_GB), whatever budget is free: 1 GiB is about 7k tokens. --no-session-cache off (a switch) do not keep a conversation's state after its turn. --no-prefix-cache off (a switch) do not checkpoint a prefill at chunk boundaries. --resident-gb 2.5 GiB for the resident prefix's anchors (RESIDENT_GB), the recurrent state (146.8 MiB) at chunk boundaries of the prompt the KV buffer holds, so the next turn of a growing conversation resumes in place, KV not copied, at any length ... --resident-stash-gb 1 GiB for the rows a short unrelated request between two turns may overwrite, copied aside and back (RESIDENT_STASH_GB; ~104 kB a row: 1 GiB holds a --resident-guest-max guest and its 512-row slack). --resident-guest-max 8192 the longest request that is a guest (RESIDENT_GUEST_MAX): opencode's title call is 1-3k tokens; a longer one replaces the resident prompt with its head pinned. --resident-tail 4 the newest anchors never evicted (the next turn resumes near the end). --resident-pin-gb 4 GiB for the head of the resident prompt a long unrelated request would otherwise cut (RESIDENT_PIN_GB): its KV rows and the anchors in it are copied aside, and a later request that shares more with that head than with the rows in ... --resident-park-gb 4 GiB for one other session's rows (RESIDENT_PARK_GB): when a request of another session (x-session-id) replaces the resident prompt, the rows past their shared head are copied aside with its newest anchors, and that session's next ... --end-anchor on the resident prefix's end anchor (END_ANCHOR): at the end of every generation the recurrent state at its last position (147 MiB, one per resident prompt), so the next request that starts with the prompt and every token the engine ... One of: on, off. --compaction continue (QSE_COMPACTION) a client's compaction request (QSE_COMPACTION, server/api/compaction.py): continue = served as the continuation of the conversation the engine holds for its session (the prefill reads only the instructions); client = as the ... One of: continue, client. --compaction-prepare on (QSE_COMPACTION_PREPARE) write an idle opencode session's summary ahead, so its /compact is answered without the engine (QSE_COMPACTION_PREPARE); a request that waits stops it at the next chunk or block. One of: on, off. --compaction-idle-s 30 (QSE_COMPACTION_IDLE_S) seconds without a request before a summary is prepared. --compaction-min-tokens 32768 (QSE_COMPACTION_MIN_TOKENS) the shortest conversation a summary is prepared for. --end-align on the end anchor for a copy whose whitespace is not the rows' (END_ALIGN, server/endalign.py): a follow-up whose copy of an earlier generation differs from what the engine wrote in whitespace alone (a tool call's trimmed parameter ... One of: on, off. --mem-ceiling-gib 70 GiB the engine may hold between requests, allocated plus the allocator's reserve (MEM_CEILING_GIB): a cache grows only while the engine stays under it less --reserve-slack-gib, and over it the caches are given back, cheapest ... --mem-peak-gib 77 GiB the engine may hold during a prefill (MEM_PEAK_GIB): the ceiling plus the workspace of a 262,144-token prompt. --reserve-slack-gib 2 GiB of free blocks the allocator may keep between requests (RESERVE_SLACK_GIB); over it they go back to the driver once a request has finished, never inside one. --prompt-token-cache 4 millions of tokens of tokenised chat messages kept, so a growing conversation's prompt is tokenised only where it is new (server/tokcache.py). 0 = tokenise every prompt whole. --session-trim off cut the engine back to the committed tokens before the session snapshot when the last verified block ran past them (end token, stop, budget) and its commit is still pending, so the put is not declined. One of: on, off. --store-boundaries 1 chunk boundaries of one prefill the state store keeps: its longest ones under the per-entry cap. 0 = every boundary, where one cold prefill's nested snapshots fill the budget and evict everything else. --prefill-heartbeat-s 5 a streamed request whose prefill has run this long gets an SSE comment (': prefill done/total') after every chunk, at most once a second, so a client and every proxy between see the stream is alive. --live-activity on the live activity on /v1/dashboard/live (states, prefill progress, timeline, the last 20 stops) at QSE_LIVE_HZ events a second while busy. off = contract 1.1 with those fields null at one event a second: the kill switch, and the ... One of: on, off. --max-prefill-rows 8192 with the prefix cache off, forward a long prompt in chunks of this many rows instead of one call; a 131k-token single forward exhausted the board. 0 = one call. --prefix-chunk 1024 tokens between prefill checkpoints, and the forward size of EVERY prefill while the prefix cache is on, the two have to agree or a warm prefill is not the same arithmetic as a cold one. --response-cache off (a switch) OPT-IN. Answer an identical (prompt, params) request from memory. --response-cache-mb 256 the response cache's budget in MiB. --response-cache-ttl 3600 seconds a response cache entry is kept. --suffix-store ~/.qwen38-spark-engine/suffix (QWEN38_SUFFIX_STORE) directory for the persistent suffix store of what this engine has read and written, which the lookup drafter reads as a second corpus. --suffix-store-readonly off (a switch) read the suffix store and never append to it: a fixed benchmark measured against a store of real traffic must not write itself into it. --suffix-store-mb 192 cap on the store, in MiB of int32 token ids (192 MiB = 48 M tokens). --disk-cache off; served: (a path) the disk tier: a directory on the NVMe for prompt-prefix state, prefixes prefilled more than once, a session's first long request, under the caches in RAM, or off (the default). --disk-cache-min-tokens 4096 the shortest prefix the disk tier writes an anchor for. --conductor-defaults builtin; served: shipped shipped, the live documents are stored as version 1 for every document the conductor's directory has no version of; builtin, the minimal built-ins stay version 0. One of: builtin, shipped. --session-spill on a live conversation on the NVMe, under the disk tier's directory: written whole at a planned stop and read back at the next start, written before another client's request evicts it, read back at its next turn. One of: on, off. --session-spill-gb 64 the session spill's own budget on the NVMe (a 256k conversation is about 27 GB as it is in the engine, about 16 GB compressed); the disk tier's free-space floor holds for both; settings.memory.session_spill overrides it live. --session-spill-codec zstd new spill blocks as byte planes compressed with zstd (exact under the agreement rule, 1.71x on a real entry; blocks on the disk are read either way). One of: zstd, off. --disk-write-budget-gb 200 the engine's NVMe writes a local day past which optional writes stop (the tier's, and the spill's but a drain and evictions of 32k+ tokens; past 1.5x only the drain); 0 = no budget; settings.memory.disk_writes.budget_gb overrides ... --session-spill-idle on write every slot's conversation of 4,096+ tokens to the NVMe once it is idle (its rows stay in RAM), so a later reclaim under memory pressure only trims it; optional under the day's write budget. One of: on, off. --session-spill-idle-s 20 how long a conversation is idle before the idle backfill writes it. --session-spill-idle-every-s 60 the least time between two idle writes of one conversation. --session-spill-resave-s 300 : an eviction, switch or idle save of a conversation whose entry was written this recently is skipped while it grew by fewer than --session-spill-resave-min-tokens (its entry stays; a restore prefills the rest); 0 = always write. --session-spill-resave-min-tokens 8192 : the growth past the entry from which such a save runs anyway. --session-spill-min-tokens 16384 the shortest resident conversation an eviction writes to the NVMe (shorter ones are the RAM park's). --disk-cache-head-anchors 4 anchors a session's first long request gets, at the grid lines below where its last user message starts (where the next session parts). --suffix-store-scope all all remembers prompts and answers, outputs only what the engine wrote. One of: all, outputs. --request-timeout 900; served: 3600 wall-clock cap on one generation, checked between blocks; 0 disables. --max-queue 8 requests allowed to wait for the engine before new ones get a 503 with Retry-After. --queue-timeout 120; served: 240 how long a request waits for the engine before a 429. --side-lane on a short request, a client's side request or a raw one, thinking off, within the two caps below, is served at the next safe point of the generation that holds the engine (on: between decode blocks and between prefill chunks ... One of: on, decode, off. --side-lane-prompt-max 2048 the longest prompt the side lane serves, in tokens. --side-lane-new-max 64 the most output tokens the side lane serves. --parallel 1 (QSE_PARALLEL) sequence slots: 1 (the default) is one sequence, as always. --side-max-len 0 (QSE_SIDE_MAX_LEN) a side slot's window in tokens; 0: --max-len, every slot the same window. --parallel-floor-gb 15 (QSE_PARALLEL_FLOOR_GB) admission: MemAvailable less the caches' growth, the requests in flight and this request's worst case must stay at or above this; a side slot is built only if it does with the slot's bytes added. --parallel-batch on (QSE_PARALLEL_BATCH) on: decoding slots verify their trees in one joint pass (lockstep rounds); off: they take turns, one verify each. One of: on, off. --parallel-draft on (QSE_PARALLEL_DRAFT) with the joint verify on: the decoding slots' draft calls in one packed pass over the drafter (on), or one after the other (off). One of: on, off. --parallel-switch-ms 0 (QSE_PARALLEL_SWITCH_MS) with side slots: the interpreter's thread switch interval in ms (0 keeps Python's 5 ms); a woken slot waits up to this long for the GIL. --parallel-cut none (QSE_PARALLEL_CUT) how a joint pass's rows are shared: share (each slot cuts its tree to a fixed share before it submits: 16 at two slots, 10 at three, 8 at four), joint (the round cuts every slot's whole tree together, best nodes first), or auto ... One of: share, joint, auto. --parallel-max-rows 0 (QSE_PARALLEL_MAX_ROWS) rows of a joint pass at most; 0 (the default): the model family's (joint_policy, else 32, the row-invariant kernels' range).: the 27B on EXL3 weights takes 64, each engine's joint rows bit for bit its own verify. --parallel-draft-rows 128 (QSE_PARALLEL_DRAFT_ROWS) rows of a packed draft pass at most: drafting decides speed only, so the drafter's pass is not held to the verify's row-invariant range; at 128, eight slots' 16-row blocks draft in one pass (32 packed two). --batch-timeout-ms 2 a joint round runs without a missing slot once the GPU turn has been idle this long. --turn-quantum-ms 50 the GPU turn goes to a waiting slot this far behind in GPU time. --parallel-settle on synchronize the device before the turn changes hands (the routers' timings then hold only their own slot's work). One of: on, off. --side-precapture off capture a side slot's verify graphs at start (on, about a minute a slot) or at their first use (off: the build takes seconds; each width's first lone round on a side slot pays its capture, a fraction of a second). One of: on, off. --side-graphs on (QSE_SIDE_GRAPHS) a side slot's own verify graphs: on (captured as --side-precapture says; most of a slot's constant bytes) or off (the slot verifies eager when it decodes alone and holds no graph pool; a joint pass is eager either way). One of: on, off. --side-slot-const-gb 0 (QSE_SIDE_SLOT_CONST_GB) a side slot's bytes beyond its window's, in the build's estimate; 0 (the default) follows --side-graphs: 7.5 GiB with it on (6.9 to 7.5 GiB allocated measured for 8,192-token slots, most of it the verify graphs' pools: 121 ... --kv-pool off (QSE_KV_POOL) on: every slot's KV window (engine attention KV and the drafters' context KV) is reserved as virtual addresses and its pages are committed as a conversation's rows are written and given back when it ends, from one pool for every ... One of: on, off. --kv-hard-floor-gb 10 (QSE_KV_HARD_FLOOR_GB) with --kv-pool on: a commit never takes MemAvailable under this (GiB); the pool gives back caches and idle conversations first, else the request is not run (admission keeps requests out at --parallel-floor-gb). --kv-margin-rows 256 (QSE_KV_MARGIN_ROWS) with --kv-pool on: rows committed past every write (a masked tile's over-read stays on mapped pages). --vision on; served: off load the checkpoint's vision tower (0.92 GB bf16) and accept image_url parts in chat requests; off refuses them with a 400. One of: on, off. --image-max-mb 20 largest image a request may send or link, after base64 decoding. --image-max-decode-pixels 64000000 largest canvas an image may declare, checked before its pixels are decoded; the processor then resizes to its own limits. --image-max-pixels 0 the processor's resize target cap in pixels (0: the checkpoint's preprocessor_config.json, e.g. 16,777,216 = 16,384 rows an image). --image-backend torchvision (QSE_IMAGE_BACKEND) the image processor's backend, pinned so the patches do not depend on what is installed (the two differ by up to two 8-bit levels after a resize). torchvision (the default, what every served measurement ran) needs torchvision ... One of: torchvision, pil. --max-images 16 images one request may send. --max-image-rows 65536 prompt rows all of a request's images may take together (one row per 2x2 block of 16-pixel patches; a 1024x1024 image is 1024 rows). --image-https on fetch https:// image URLs (off: data: URLs only). One of: on, off. --image-https-private off let https image URLs reach loopback, private and link-local addresses (off: public hosts only). One of: on, off. --image-fetch-timeout 15 seconds for a whole https image download, redirects included. --image-cache-mb 512 encoded images kept on the device by content, so a conversation that sends an image again does not encode it again. --image-act-gb 6 admission: an image whose encode would need more than this (the tower's byte math, engine/vision.py) is refused with a 400. --usage-default on (QSE_USAGE_DEFAULT) a streamed request that sends no stream_options gets usage, timings and metrics on its finish chunk (on, the default: Open WebUI asks for include_usage only when a model's Usage capability is ticked), or nothing, as before (off). ... One of: on, off. --usage-context client (QSE_USAGE_CONTEXT) usage.prompt_tokens counts the client's prompt (client, the default) or the full context occupied after replay (engine). One of: client, engine. --usage-ledger off; served: (a path) the SQLite usage ledger's path, or off (the default). --conductor-config off the conductor's config directory (versioned profiles, router, roles, packages and its journal, TandemApp's tandemapp/conductor/), or off (the default). --backends off off, the only value this engine takes: any other stops the start with one line. --usage-retention-days 400 days the usage ledger keeps its rows (at least 400). --trust-loopback on (--no-trust-loopback turns it off) a request from loopback with no X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP header (the box's own watchdog, row3, gate, soak) needs no token for /metrics, the full /health and the cache routes once an admin password or metrics token is set. --dashboard-login off (QSE_DASHBOARD_LOGIN) on, with an admin password (QSE_ADMIN_TOKEN) set: /v1/dashboard/* needs the admin token or a session too (the page has no sign-in screen yet). off, the default: the dashboard's read API answers without a token. One of: on, off. --setup off (a switch) setup mode (docs/setup.md, ops/start.sh --setup): no served model is loaded; the Setup Guide's API /v1/setup/* and Wren, its assistant, alone (tandem setup in a terminal, or TandemApp's Setup page pointed at this engine). --fake-engine off (a switch) the e2e: no weights, no GPU, a deterministic CPU token source (server/fake_engine.py) behind the real handler, auth, ledger, metrics and logs. --fake-tps 200 with --fake-engine: tokens a second it writes. --fake-prefill-tps 0 with --fake-engine: the prefill rate of a FAKE_SLOW_PREFILL prompt (0 = 2,000 tokens a second). --fake-load-s 0 with --fake-engine: a load of this many seconds before the port opens, writing the load's phases as the real engine does. --structured-outputs on (--no-structured-outputs turns it off) serve response_format json_object / json_schema and structured_outputs (regex, choice, json) as masks over the target's rows, exact under speculation. --log-content off (a switch) let exception messages that quote a request into the log. --log-request-keys off (a switch) one [body] line per request with the parameter names and the scalar values of the non-content ones (model, stream, max_tokens, temperature,...); never messages, prompt, tools or stop strings. --verbose off (a switch); served: on more log lines. --stage none serve the layers [LO, HI) of --model as one of two stage processes: 0:k is the front stage, k:layers the tail, the one a client talks to. --link-listen none with --stage: wait for the other stage on this address (an IP literal). --link-peer none with --stage: connect to the other stage at this address (an IP literal). --stage-graphs on with --stage: a stage whose family captures graphs for its passes captures its own (on), or runs every pass eager (off). One of: on, off. --stage-caches off with --stage: keep state on both stages under one key: the prefix, session and resident caches, the disk tier and side slots; off: one sequence, nothing kept. One of: on, off. --stage-snapshots-gb 2 with --stage-caches on, the front stage: memory for the states it keeps, a slot. --stage-cache-dir none with --stage-caches on, the front stage: the directory for its half of what the tail's disk tier keeps (none: a state read from the tail's disk is rebuilt or missed). --stage-cache-gb 32 with --stage-cache-dir: the directory's size; the files unused longest go first. --link-key-file none with --stage: the key both stages share, a file of mode 0600 with at least 32 bytes.

docs.title: The installer
docs.text: install.sh [options]; install.md explains the install.

docs.title: install.sh options
docs.text:
Option What it does --dir DIR install directory (default ~/TandemLLM) --port PORT the API port (default 8000) --host ADDR the address to bind (default 127.0.0.1; 0.0.0.0 serves the LAN, with no auth on the OpenAI routes) --ref REF the engine release: tag, branch or commit (default v0.16.0) --repo URL the git repository to clone (default the public repository) --hf-token TOKEN a Hugging Face token (or set HF_TOKEN; a stored 'hf auth login' works too) --no-corpus skip the lookup corpus (the lookup drafter then copies from the conversation only) --no-start install and configure, but do not start the engine --with-chat the chat (beta) too: the conductor (router, user memory, packages), its small models, and TandemApp's TandemNode with chatd, the Chat tab's service; needs --app-wheel (a re-run keeps the TandemApp it installed). Without it a new install serves the engine alone (no page, no chat) and a re-run keeps the mode --app-wheel FILE with --with-chat: TandemApp's wheel, a local file (tandemapp-*.whl), into this install's venv (the engine's pins held) --app-wheel-sha256 HEX the wheel's sha256, checked before it is installed --engine-only the engine alone, a new install's default; on a re-run it turns the chat off --setup set up instead of a model now: install the code and Wren's model only, then start setup mode (the Setup API, /v1/setup/*, for TandemApp's Setup page; docs/setup.md); 127.0.0.1 unless --host says otherwise --force-setup with --setup, on a directory that already has a configured engine --systemd also install a systemd user unit, tandemllm.service (off by default) --runtime-only the engine's source and Python environment only: no weights, no corpus, no config, no start (what TandemApp's Add Spark wizard installs on a new node) --update an install with its config: the source at --ref and the venv, then the config rendered again from the new release with this install's keys as they are; no weights, no corpus, no start (tandem remote upgrade runs it) --no-fetch take --ref from what DIR/src already has; no git fetch --no-pair no pairing window at the end; a new install then binds 127.0.0.1 and writes no HTTP token lock (bin/tandem pair opens a window later: docs/pairing.md) --retire-backends on a re-run whose config sets QSE_BACKENDS (the relay the engine had before engine API 1.8): once its backends are on TandemApp's controller, comment the line out (dated) and go on; the backends' database stays --yes, -y non-interactive: answer yes to every question --dry-run print every step and command, change nothing --uninstall stop the engine, remove the unit and DIR (the weights stay in the HF cache) -h, --help this text

Environment variables the installer reads: TANDEM_REF, TANDEM_REPO, TANDEM_DIR, TANDEM_PORT, TANDEM_HOST, HF_TOKEN, HF_HOME.

docs.title: TandemApp
docs.text: tandem-app, tandem-app launch and tandem-app hostcollect are TandemApp's commands: TandemApp's docs lists their flags.

docs.title: The service scripts
docs.text:
command what it does bin/tandem start\|stop\|restart\|status\|smoke\|logs the installed engine's control script (install.md) ops/start.sh starts the engine from serve.env, waits for /health, drops the weights' page cache, loads the roles ops/stop.sh [seconds] SIGTERM, the drain, then a kill only after the wait ops/watchdog.sh one health check, for cron every minute ops/hold.sh <minutes> <command> a command with the board to itself, then the service back ops/gate.sh <label> [--profile F] the release gate ops/make-secrets.sh [--admin] [--rotate] the metrics token; --admin adds the admin password ops/roles.sh load\|up\|down\|settle roles beside the engine, through the residency planner . ops/engines.sh; engine_pids every engine process on the board

The scripts in ops/ and the installed control script.

docs.title: Measurement and maintenance tools
docs.text:
The tools/ directory holds about 180 scripts: kernels, quantisers, probes, checks and benches. The ones these docs refer to are listed here; each prints its own --help.

tool what it does tools/row3.py the benchmark row, N runs through one server, with --compare tools/block_ab.py the in-process A/B for changes that keep the bits tools/forced_bench.py the teacher-forced bench tools/verify_spec.py the agreement gate with its near-tie rule tools/flagoff_identity.py the identity gate with the new flags off tools/api_text_check.py 13 plain requests against the current release tools/client_smoke.py the request shapes real clients send tools/verify_curve.py the verify prices StairCut cuts on tools/quant_nvfp4.py, quant_head.py the quantisers tools/quality_gate.py the quality gate tools/calib_corpus.py, build_corpus.py the calibration text and the lookup corpus tools/mem_audit.py the memory a configuration holds tools/disk_cache_live.py, disk_restore_check.py the disk tier's live and bit-exact checks tools/session_spill_check.py the session spill's bit-exact check tools/lane_check.py the side lane on the real engine tools/tandem_eval.py the conductor's evaluation suites tools/conductor_policy.py the monitor's policy schema and its check tools/shadow_ab.py, shadow_measure.py the shadow reader's cost and read rate tools/voice_replay.py a recorded session's lines through the voice tools/parallel_load.py agent-like sessions over several backends tools/package_check.sh the wheel builds and installs without torch tools/gen_reference.py the reference tables

The tools these docs refer to.

docs.title: Reference: HTTP
docs.text: This page lists every route, every header and every error of the engine's server. TandemApp's proxy speaks the same API for clients and has its own routes, headers and errors, and so does its extension inside the engine: TandemApp's docs lists them. The tables are written in tools/http_ref.py, and tools/gen_reference.py --check compares them with the code in the tests: a route a handler tests, a header name or an error type the code uses that is missing here, or a row the code no longer has, fails the check.

docs.title: Who may call what
docs.text:
The admin password is the admin token, QSE_ADMIN_TOKEN in secrets.env. It is not set by default. Then every route below answers anyone who reaches the port, and only /metrics keeps the metrics token when one is set. With a password set, an admin route needs it as a bearer header or a dashboard session (a cookie the token buys). A request from the machine itself (loopback, no proxy headers) needs neither, because the watchdog and the measurement tools rely on that (--trust-loopback).

The OpenAI routes are open on the engine, with or without a password. The table below names the labels the route tables use.

docs.title: Who may call a route: the labels of the routes' who column
docs.text: label who may call open anyone who reaches the port admin the admin rule: anyone while no admin password is set; with one, the admin token, a dashboard session, or a tool on the machine itself admin-bearer as admin, but the token only as a bearer header, never the session cookie dash the dashboard rule: anyone unless a password is set and the dashboard login is on metrics the metrics token when one is set, else as admin session only under a session address, /s/<token>/... key anyone until the first user key exists; then a user key, except from the machine itself collect the collect token, from every address

docs.title: The engine's routes
docs.text: the table below lists the engine server's routes. A route the server does not know answers 404. A route TandemApp serves answers 404 not_on_engine on a headless engine, and the page 404 no_ui; in chat mode the extension serves them. The proxy's routes without --backends answer 404 with a message that names the flag, and the decision routes without decision models as an unknown route. The table below adds the status responder, which answers while the engine is stopped.

docs.title: The engine server's routes
docs.text: route who what POST /v1/chat/completions open A chat completion, streamed as server-sent events or not. Body: OpenAI's chat body: model, messages, tools, stream, max_tokens and the other fields of the API fields. Answer: chat.completion, or chat.completion.chunk events and [DONE]; usage carries prompt_tokens_details.hidden_tokens for the conductor's notes. POST /v1/completions open A plain text completion. Body: prompt, max_tokens and the sampling fields. Answer: text_completion, or its chunks and [DONE]. GET /v1/models open The model list: TandemLLM alone with the conductor on, else the served name. Answer: {object: list, data: [...]}, and decision_models beside data when decision models are served. GET /v1/models/{id} open One model card: the engine's or a decision model's. Answer: the card, or 404 model_not_found. GET /v1/replica/identity open What two engines compare before they serve one model as replicas: the code, the family, the weights, drafters, rows and tokenizer by content, and the decode settings (SRV-741). Follows the caller rule of /v1/models. Answer: {identity: 1, served_model, base_model, version, code, family, layers, profile, weights, drafters, rows, tokenizer, decode, max_len, stage}; 503 identity_pending until the first call's computation ends. GET /health open Whether the server takes work. The full body follows the admin rule; anyone else gets the status alone. Also /healthz and /v1/health. Answer: {status: ok\|draining}; the full body adds model, uptime, inflight, the queue, limits, sampling, cache, memory and parallel; 503 while draining. GET /metrics metrics The Prometheus families of the metrics reference. Answer: Prometheus text format. GET /metrics/up open One gauge, qse_up, so a scraper can tell an engine that is down from a wrong token. Answer: qse_up 1, or 0 while draining. GET /v1/cache/stats admin Every cache's counters. Answer: the cache report /health carries. GET /v1/cache/memory?pools=1 admin The engine's memory by owner against what it held once loaded: each slot's anchors, end anchor, stash, pin and park, the store, the KV pool's pages and what no cache holds (SPD-257). pools=1 adds the allocator's segments by pool; it walks every block. Answer: {allocated, reserved, load, caches, by_owner, unattributed, limits, kv_pool, allocator_pools?}. POST /v1/cache/peek admin Where a chat's rows are before it is sent: the body is rendered as a request would be, the session's router notes are replayed, and the cache tiers are asked without running the model (SRV-349). Body: a chat body (messages, tools, the effort fields) and session. Answer: {tier: resident\|ram_park\|ram_snapshot\|nvme_spill\|disk_tier\|none, cached_tokens, reread_tokens, reread_eta_ms, tokens, restore_ms, session}; 409 while a request holds the engine. POST /v1/cache/prewarm admin Reads a conversation the peek finds on the NVMe back into the engine while nothing runs or waits, so its next request resumes at the end anchor. Body: as /v1/cache/peek. Answer: {prewarmed, why?, restore?} and the peek's fields; 409 while busy. POST /v1/tokenize open Exact token counts with the model's own chat template, split by part; nothing runs on the GPU (SRV-347). With ids: true also the ids, the chat prompt's or the text's as /v1/completions reads it (SPD-249). 240 a minute from one address. Body: {messages, tools?, ids?} or {text, ids?}. Answer: {tokens, parts: {system, tools, messages}, ids?}. POST /v1/cache/clear?tier=ram\|disk\|all admin-bearer Empties the caches in memory (ram, the default), the disk tier and the session spill (disk), or both (all). Nothing else is reset. Answer: the cache report after the clear; 400 for another tier. POST /v1/cache/release admin-bearer Gives back memory the engine holds idle, cheapest first: free allocator blocks and caches while slot 0 is idle, the small models, idle side conversations, slot 0's idle conversation (to the NVMe first). chatd asks it before a sandbox waits (SRV-483). Body: {bytes}. Answer: what each step gave back and the total. GET /dashboard/ open No page: every engine answers 404 no_ui under /dashboard (engine API 1.8); TandemApp's controller serves the page. Answer: 404 no_ui. GET /v1/dashboard/summary?from=&to=&tz=&model=&client=&backend=&user=&internal= dash The Usage view's totals for a range. Answer: summary.schema.json in contracts/engine-api-v1/dashboard. GET /v1/dashboard/usage?bucket=hour\|day&from=&to=&tz=&model=&client=&backend=&user=&internal= dash Tokens, requests and cost per hour or day. Answer: usage.schema.json. GET /v1/dashboard/requests?limit=&before=&finish=&model=&client=&backend=&user=&internal= dash Recent request rows of the usage ledger, newest first. Answer: requests.schema.json. GET /v1/dashboard/system dash The machine, the engine, the memory plan and the slots; the proxy's mode is always off. Answer: system.schema.json. GET /v1/dashboard/live dash What each request is doing now, as server-sent events. Answer: live.schema.json events. GET /v1/dashboard/logs?level=&grep=&backlog=&since=&follow= dash The log: a backlog of up to 5,000 lines, then live lines as server-sent events; Last-Event-ID resumes; follow=0 answers JSON once. Answer: logs-line.schema.json events, or logs-json.schema.json; 429 past four streams at once. GET /v1/dashboard/logs/export dash The whole log ring as one text file: a header with the version, the commit, the uptime, the time of export and the line count, then every line the ring holds, at all levels, oldest first. It takes no stream place. Answer: text/plain as an attachment named tandemllm-<version>-<time>.log. GET /v1/dashboard/metrics dash The /metrics page under the dashboard's rule, for the Performance view. Answer: Prometheus text format. GET /v1/dashboard/parallel?since= dash Every request in flight on the engine. Answer: parallel.schema.json. GET /v1/dashboard/session open Whether a sign-in exists and is needed. Answer: {authenticated, login, password_set, expires_at}. POST /v1/dashboard/session open The sign-in, with a password set and the login on: sets the qse_dash cookie. Five failures a minute from one address and the sixth gets a 429. Body: {token}. Answer: the session; 401 for a wrong token. DELETE /v1/dashboard/session open Signs this session out. Answer: the session, signed out. * /v1/conductor/* admin The conductor's documents, journal, sessions and memory, served by the extension in chat mode (TandemApp's docs lists them). Reads follow the dashboard rule, writes and every memory route the admin rule. 404 not_on_engine on a headless engine. * /v1/setup/* admin The Setup Guide's API (docs/setup.md): the model registry, the box, the memory estimate, the review plan, the apply and reset jobs and Wren. Every POST must also be same-origin JSON: 415 for another content type, 403 for another origin. In setup mode (--setup) these, the session and /health are the only routes that answer. * /v1/config/* open 404 not_on_engine on every engine (engine API 1.8): other backends sit behind TandemApp's controller. Answer: 404 not_on_engine. POST /v1/collect/{backend} open 404 not_on_engine on every engine (engine API 1.8): the host collector is TandemApp's controller's. Answer: 404 not_on_engine. * /v1/chat-app open 404 not_on_engine on every engine (engine API 1.8), and every path under it: TandemApp's controller serves the Chat tab's service. The body is not read. Answer: 404 not_on_engine. POST /v1/systemone admin Typed decisions from the decision models, in the engine's idle window. /v1/predict is the same route. Only with QWEN38_DECIDER_MODELS. Body: {state, model?, questions: {id: {type, instructions, criteria?}}, task?, lang?}. Answer: {model, answers, usage, routing, latency_ms, path}. POST /v1/predict admin The same as /v1/systemone. Body: as /v1/systemone. Answer: as /v1/systemone. GET /readyz open Whether a decision model is loaded and warm. Answer: 200, or 503 with the reason. GET /v1/laya open What the Laya route takes and answers, its limits, and whether it is on. The Laya, library and session memory routes below are the extension's in chat mode (TandemApp's docs has their shapes); a headless engine answers them 404 not_on_engine. Answer: a description of the route. POST /v1/laya/ask open A typed answer from Laya on one text or many, for the model's own scripts; rate-limited. Body: {question, choices \| scale \| neither, text \| texts, threshold?, model?, deadline_ms?}. Answer: {label, p, sure, probs, model, ms, ...}, or {answers: [...]} for texts. POST /v1/laya/drive/end open Ends a playtest driver session and writes its journal row. Body: the session's summary. Answer: the row. GET /v1/laya/kit/{file} open A file of the playtest kit the model copies into a project. Answer: the file. OPTIONS /v1/laya/* open A browser's CORS preflight for the Laya routes, which the engine asks the extension for. Every other path answers OPTIONS with 501. Answer: 204 with the extension's CORS headers. GET /v1/library open The package library: every enabled skill's name, description and classes. Answer: the list and the two routes below. GET /v1/library/search?q=&k=&class= open BM25 search over the skills, best first (k from 1 to 20, default 5). Answer: [{name, description, score}]. GET /v1/library/{name} open One skill's text and its reference. Answer: {name, description, classes, body, reference}. GET /s/{token}/v1/memory session The memory index this session sees. The /s/{token}/ prefix also serves the library and Laya routes, filed to the session. Answer: the notes' index lines. GET /s/{token}/v1/memory/search?q=&k= session Memory notes that match, best first (k from 1 to 10). Answer: [{id, kind, scope, status, title, score}]. GET /s/{token}/v1/memory/{id} session One note. Answer: {id, title, kind, scope, status, body, ...}. POST /s/{token}/v1/memory session Writes, changes or archives a note, with the fields of the hidden memory block. Body: {op, scope, kind, title, tags, body, id, reason}. Answer: {op, id, title, ...}, or 422 with the reason as the type.

docs.title: The status responder beside the engine
docs.text: server route answer ops/engine_status.py GET /v1/models 200 with the engine's last model list and its state, while the engine is away ops/engine_status.py GET /dashboard/ 503 with a page that says why the engine is away and opens the dashboard when it is back ops/engine_status.py * any other path 503 provider_unavailable with Retry-After and the state as engine_<state>

docs.title: Request fields of the engine's own
docs.text:
Two fields of a chat or completion request concern the wait for memory (waiting for memory). The engine reads them; What the API supports lists the OpenAI fields.

  • tandem.priority: "high", "normal" or "low", the chat's place in the line for memory and in the order the KV pool's reclaim takes idle conversations. Any other value, or none, is normal (0.15.3).
  • wait_for_memory: true, in the body or in its tandem object: a request without a stream waits for memory up to QSE_MEM_WAIT_S instead of --queue-timeout, as the header X-Tandem-Wait-For-Memory: 1 asks (0.15.3).

docs.title: Headers
docs.text: the table below lists every header the engine reads or writes beyond the ones HTTP itself needs. in is a header the server reads, out one it writes.

docs.title: Every header the engine reads or writes (both: TandemApp's controller too)
docs.text: header direction, where meaning X-Tandem both, both raw, shadow or on: lowers the conductor's mode for one request; the response says which mode ran X-Tandem-Profile both, both picks a conductor profile; the response names the profile that ran; an unknown name is a 400 X-Tandem-Memory in, engine off: no memory note is read or written; read: reads only, a block the model writes is hidden and dropped X-Tandem-Probe in, engine off takes the request out of the probe snapshots X-Tandem-User in, engine a proxy's user name for the memory notes, honoured from loopback or QWEN38_MEMORY_PROXIES X-Tandem-Relay-Id in, engine a proxy's id for a relayed request, for the live counts; a relayed request without X-Tandem-User touches no memory X-Tandem-Parent in, engine the request a call of TandemLLM to itself serves; the row becomes client kind internal X-Tandem-Worker in, engine 1 on an agent's worker request: its session comes back, so it is never a guest, and its rows go to the NVMe rather than away while it waits X-Tandem-Parent-Session in, engine a worker's parent session (the chat's): for 600 s after the worker's last request the parent's rows go to the NVMe rather than away, and its return tries slot 0 first X-Tandem-Regenerate in, engine 1 serves the request as a regenerate (sampled, a fresh seed); 0 turns the detection off for it X-Tandem-Images-Left-Out out, engine how many earlier images were left out of the prompt X-Tandem-Wait out, engine memory, on a response that waited for memory before its prefill; its stream says so every 15 s X-Tandem-Wait-For-Memory in, engine 1: a request not streamed waits for memory up to QSE_MEM_WAIT_S, as wait_for_memory: true in the body does, instead of a 503 after the queue timeout X-Engine-Stop out, engine pattern-stop(<label>) on a response without a stream that a stop pattern ended x-session-id in, both opencode's session id: the router's session and the caches' session key X-Conversation-Id in, both a conversation id for clients that send no session field; read after the body's own ids X-OpenWebUI-Chat-Id in, both Open WebUI's chat id (a connection header with {{CHAT_ID}}): the router's session for that chat X-QSE-Client in, engine dashboard marks the dashboard's own requests (client kind dashboard) X-Real-IP in, both set by a reverse proxy; a request that carries it is never trusted as local; the sign-in's rate limit counts per address X-Forwarded-For in, both as X-Real-IP: a request that carries it is never trusted as local X-Forwarded-Proto in, both https makes the session cookie Secure, and the notes' {tandem_url} https X-Forwarded-Host in, engine the host the notes' {tandem_url} names, unless QWEN38_TANDEM_URL sets it X-Decider-Deadline-Ms in, engine how long a decision request waits for the idle window (default 30,000, at most 120,000) X-Decider-Window in, engine in_decode is refused: decisions run in the idle window only X-Accel-Buffering out, both no, on every stream, so nginx sends each event at once X-Content-Type-Options out, both nosniff on the dashboard's static files Authorization in, both Bearer: the admin token, the metrics token, the collect token or a proxy user key, by route; the engine's OpenAI routes ignore it and file the request under a hash of it User-Agent in, both the client kind in the ledger: open-webui, opencode, openai-sdk, curl, other (a Hermes-shaped body: hermes) Last-Event-ID in, both resumes the log stream after that line Retry-After out, both with a 503 (queue full, memory gate, draining, a full backend), a 429, or a decision model that is loading WWW-Authenticate out, both Bearer, with a 401 Set-Cookie out, both qse_dash, the dashboard session: HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure behind https X-Tandem-Pair-Key in, engine the pairing window key (run/remote/pair-local.key): tandem pair opens and closes a window with it, from the machine itself

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Errors are OpenAI-shaped:

{"error": {"message": "max_tokens must be at least 1", "type": "invalid_request_error",
           "param": "max_tokens", "code": null}}

A 400 names the field or the message part it refuses in param. A refusal the client can retry (a full queue, the memory gate, a server that drains) has the type server_busy, the status in code, and a Retry-After header. A refusal after a stream opened (a queue timeout, a prompt too long, the memory gate) ends the stream with a chunk whose finish_reason is "error" and which carries the error object, then [DONE]. The decision routes keep their own body, {"type": "error", "error": {"type", "message"}}. The tables below list every status and type: the first explains the common ones, the second lists every other type the code answers, with the code's own message.

docs.title: The errors explained
docs.text: status error.type or code when 400 invalid_request_error a request the engine will not serve as asked: error.param names the field (messages, a role, max_tokens, tools, an image part, a prompt too long, a body that is not JSON or not an object) 400 bad_request a dashboard or conductor query that does not parse (a level, a range, a number) 400 stage_text_only a request with images on the tail stage of a split model (--stage), as error.code beside invalid_request_error 400 confirm_required a setup reset without the confirmation its level asks for (true, or the typed word) 401 unauthorized a guarded route without the token or the session it needs, once an admin password is set; a wrong collect token 403 local_only, window_key opening or closing a pairing window (POST /v1/engine/pair/open, /close) from another machine, or without the window key 404 not_found no such route, or a route whose part is off on this server (the conductor, the proxy, the decision models) 404 not_on_engine a route TandemApp serves (the conductor, its library, memory and Laya, the backends) on an engine where no extension serves it 404 no_pairing a pairing route on a process that serves no pairing 404 no_ui the page, on every engine: TandemApp's controller serves it 404 model_not_found a model id no backend serves, or one two backends serve (the message names the prefixed forms) (code model_not_found) 409 busy, not_loaded, role_off an action that needs a role or a decision model in another state, or a role the roles document switches off (role_off) 409 stage_front any route but /health on the front stage of a split model (--stage): requests go to the tail stage 422 invalid_request_error a value the schema refuses: a config field (error.field), a field an environment variable locks (error.variable), a decision request's fields 429 with Retry-After server_busy a request without a stream that waited --queue-timeout for the engine 429 with Retry-After too_many a fifth log or live stream at once; a sixth failed sign-in in a minute 429 with Retry-After rate_limited /v1/tokenize past its 240 calls a minute from one address; a pairing route past 20 a minute from one address 500 internal_error a bug: the message is the exception's; the request is in the log 500 internal a PATCH /v1/engine/settings that raised: the message is the exception's; the call is journaled 500 extension_error a route of the extension that raised: the extension's bug, in the engine's log 501 none OPTIONS on any path but the Laya routes 503 with Retry-After server_busy the queue is full, the server is draining, or the memory gate or the admission by bytes cannot make room 503 with Retry-After memory_wait_timeout a request that waited for memory to its bound: --queue-timeout without a stream, QSE_MEM_WAIT_S streamed or with wait_for_memory; a stream that opened while it waited ends with it as an error event (type server_busy, Retry-After: 30) 503 with Retry-After setup_mode any route but the dashboard, /health, /v1/models and /v1/setup/* on a box in setup mode (Retry-After: 60) 503 with Retry-After warming, loading, refused, failed, not_loaded, busy_decoding a decision request while the model loads, was refused memory, failed, or the engine kept decoding past the deadline 503 with Retry-After identity_pending the replica identity while the engine computes it, once after the start (Retry-After: 1) 503 with Retry-After stage_down a completion on the tail stage of a split model while its link to the front stage is down (Retry-After: 5); a request in flight when the link fails ends with 500 and the same word in its message 503 with Retry-After engine_failed a completion after the engine's CUDA context was lost: the sentence says so, the watchdog restarts the engine (Retry-After: 60) 503 with Retry-After provider_unavailable the status responder while the engine is stopped, starting or held (code engine_<state>) 529 overloaded_error a decision request the runtime could not take

docs.title: Every other error type the code answers, with its status and the code's own message ({...} is a value)
docs.text: error.type or code status message where active_profile 409 {...} is the running setup: switch to another model first, or remove it after the switch server/setup/remove.py active_unknown 409 . server/setup_api.py browser_only 400 level 1 (the setup progress and Wren's chat) is the browser's own: the page clears it server/setup_api.py invalid_combination 422 server/setup/estimate.py invalid_level 422 level is 2, 3, 4 or 5 server/setup_api.py invalid_request 422 remove takes profiles, confirm and dry_run server/setup/remove.py, server/setup_api.py invalid_selection 422 the body must be a JSON object server/setup/estimate.py, server/setup_api.py invalid_split 422 split.{...}: server/setup/split.py invalid_value 422 {...}.{...}: server/setup/estimate.py job_running 409 job {...} runs; one setup job at a time server/setup_api.py not_installed 404 {...} has no weights on this box server/setup/remove.py not_retryable 409 job {...} is {...}: only a failed or rolled back job is tried again server/setup_api.py not_running 409 server/engine_routes.py off_step 422 {...}: a multiple of {...}, not {...} server/setup/estimate.py out_of_range 422 {...}: a whole number from {...} to {...} server/setup/estimate.py shared 409 {...}'s folder is also {...}'s; remove them together server/setup/remove.py timeout 408 the request body stopped arriving server/app.py too_large 413 a setup request body is at most {...} KiB server/api/http_body.py, server/setup_api.py unknown_component 400 no tool {...} for {...} server/setup/estimate.py unknown_device 400 no device preset {...} for {...} server/setup/estimate.py unknown_field 422 unknown field {...}; reset takes level, confirm and dry_run server/setup/estimate.py, server/setup_api.py unknown_model 400, 404 no model {...} in models/ server/setup/estimate.py, server/setup_api.py unknown_profile 400 no weight profile {...} for {...} server/setup/estimate.py unsafe 409 {...} is not removed: server/setup/remove.py

docs.title: Reference: metrics and the usage ledger
Prometheus metrics
docs.text:
GET /metrics serves the families below in the Prometheus text format, to anyone while no token is set, else behind the metrics or admin token, or to a request from the machine itself. ops/monitoring/ has a scrape configuration, alert rules with their tests, and a Grafana dashboard generated by tools/grafana_dashboard.py. With the metrics token set, a scrape job needs it as a bearer token:

- job_name: tandemllm
  authorization: {type: Bearer, credentials_file: /etc/prometheus/tandem-metrics.token}
  static_configs: [{targets: ['gpu-host:8000']}]

The engine's families never count a relayed request. The table lists every family the engine registers with a literal name in the code; families built at scrape time from a table (the cache families by cache label) are listed by their prefix in the help text of the page itself. The extension's families (qse_conductor_*, marked "owner": "ext" in contracts/engine-api-v1/metrics-families.json), the proxy's and the host collector's are in TandemApp's docs.

docs.title: Prometheus families the engine registers (the extension's are in TandemApp's docs)
docs.text: Metric Type, labels What it counts qse_requests_total counter, finish_reason generations that finished, by the reason they finished qse_request_success_total counter generations that finished on the model's own stop token or the caller's token budget qse_prompt_tokens_total counter prompt tokens accepted, including tokens served from a cache qse_generation_tokens_total counter tokens written by the engine qse_errors_total counter, type exceptions that ended a generation, by exception class qse_images_left_out_total counter a conversation's earlier images left out of a request over the image caps (server/images.py) qse_time_to_first_token_seconds histogram arrival of the request to its first token, queue wait included qse_time_per_output_token_seconds histogram gap between two tokens of one generation. qse_e2e_request_latency_seconds histogram arrival of the request to the end of its stream, queue wait included qse_spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total counter drafted tokens the target agreed with. The token the target writes itself is not counted here, so accepted over drafted is the draft acceptance rate qse_spec_decode_num_draft_tokens_total counter tokens proposed by the drafter, anchor excluded qse_spec_decode_num_drafts_total counter blocks the drafter proposed qse_spec_accept_per_block histogram tokens committed by one verified block, the target's own token included qse_draft_width_chosen_total counter, width blocks proposed at each width, anchor included. qse_verify_seconds histogram one verify pass over a draft block, as the decode loop paid for it qse_draft_seconds histogram one call to the drafter, lookup and block drafter together qse_ext_errors_total counter, hook extension hooks that failed (raised, a wrong shape, an act out of place); the request went on without them, by hook qse_requests_running gauge generations the engine is working on qse_requests_waiting gauge requests holding a socket and waiting for the engine qse_requests_refused_total counter, reason requests turned away with a Retry-After before the engine saw them qse_cache_misses_total counter, cache prefix lookups that found nothing qse_cache_evictions_total counter, cache entries dropped to stay inside the byte budget qse_cache_bytes gauge, cache bytes held by each cache qse_ngram_table_cache_hits_total counter n-gram table rows served from the hot-row cache qse_ngram_table_cache_misses_total counter n-gram table rows read from disk (O_DIRECT) for a hot-row cache miss qse_ngram_table_blocks_read_total counter 4 KiB blocks docs.title: The usage ledger
docs.text:
server/api/ledger.py writes one SQLite row per request: counts, timings, the finish reason, the cache source, a client id. Never the prompt, the answer, a tool name or argument, a conversation id, the user field, an IP address or a raw token. Refused requests (503, 429) and rejected ones (400) are rows too, with null token fields, so the request count is honest.

It never slows or fails a request. A row is put on a bounded queue (10,000), a writer thread commits in batches at most every second, and a disk error drops that batch, counts it and logs it at most once a minute. Rows older than --usage-retention-days (at least 400) are deleted once a day, and once an ISO week an online backup goes beside the file, the newest 8 kept. The server takes the path from --usage-ledger only, never from the environment, so a benchmark server started with serve.env exported never writes the operator's ledger. Migrations are forward only and in place, and keep every row.

The conductor's journal shares the file: conductor_events has 53 columns (id, ts_ms, request_id, session_key, kind, task, tier, mode, sp, rule, trigger, score, decision, action, cap, tier1_model, question_id, probabilities, tier1_ms, hidden_text_id, hidden_tokens, tokens_at_cut, position, outcome, next_checker, policy_version, client_kind, model, profile, profile_version, router_version, class_id, confidence, source, kept, stages, classifier_ms, effort, budget, budget_source, thinking, decisions, injected, replayed, shadow, digest, label, label_note, labelled_at, acted, changed, detail, extra), and conductor_texts keeps every hidden text once, by its hash.

A row's speed figures follow the benchmark row's formula, and a replay or a side-lane request has no decode rate. A relayed request has null queue, prefill, blocks, draft counts and cache source unless a plugin reported them, in which case l2_join says how the row was joined. A quick look:

sqlite3 ~/.qwen38-spark-engine/usage/ledger.sqlite3 \
  "select datetime(ts_ms/1000,'unixepoch','localtime'), finish_reason, prompt_tokens,
          completion_tokens, round(decode_tps,1), cache_source from requests order by id desc limit 10"

docs.title: Reference: environment and configuration
docs.text: TandemEngine reads four families of settings. Engine switches are QWEN38_* variables, read through one registry. Server settings are command-line flags (Command-line reference); ops/start.sh builds them from ops/serve.env, and a few QSE_* variables set flags' defaults or serve the scripts. The installer and the service scripts read a few TANDEM_* variables. And the conductor's behaviour lives in its versioned documents, which the dashboard edits. The QWEN38_* knobs the extension reads, and the variables of TandemApp's proxy, collector and plugins, are in TandemApp's docs.

The most used: QSE_CONDUCTOR_CONFIG, QSE_USAGE_LEDGER, QSE_DISK_CACHE and QSE_BACKENDS name the conductor's directory, the ledger, the disk tier's directory and the proxy's config database; ops/start.sh passes them to the service only, so a benchmark server started with serve.env exported never writes them. QSE_DASHBOARD_LOGIN turns the dashboard login on. QSE_ADMIN_TOKEN and QSE_METRICS_TOKEN live in secrets.env, which ops/make-secrets.sh writes.

The wait for memory (Waiting for memory) reads these, with their code defaults: QSE_MEM_WAIT_S (10,800) is the longest wait in seconds of a streamed request, or of one that sends wait_for_memory: true; QSE_PARALLEL_FLOOR_GB (15) is the floor the admission keeps MemAvailable at, the same as --parallel-floor-gb; QSE_KV_HARD_FLOOR_GB (10) is the floor the KV pool's commits keep, the same as --kv-hard-floor-gb; QSE_GUARD_MARGIN_GB (5) is the margin each floor holds under the largest step the engine takes between two checks; QSE_KV_ADMIT_ROWS (8,192) is the part of max_tokens the admission reserves KV pages for, 0 for all of it; QSE_KV_RECOMPUTE (on) lets a lane the pool refuses give way and go on later; QSE_PEAK_STRICT (0) set to 1 makes a lone request that the memory gate refuses wait too.

document what it holds edited on profiles one document per profile: mode, decisions, task modes and caps, thinking, ui, outcomes, library, memory, shadow Profiles router the classes and their policy, the classifier stages and thresholds, the structural rules, side shapes, outcomes, library Routing packages every package: source, switch, limits, flags Packages roles every role's contract Profiles, Roles settings the default profile, transcripts, the disk tier, memory notes and the writer Memory, Profiles deciders the decision models, their questions, Laya for scripts Deciders residency the floor, the margin, the settle time, the load order, the claims Profiles, Residency monitor the session monitor's policy (version 0 is ops/supervisor.yaml) Monitor harness the harness's settings per backend, behind the proxy Backends

The conductor's versioned documents.

A document is JSON, checked against the conductor's schema (GET /v1/conductor/meta serves it, and TandemApp's contracts/conductor-v1/ holds a copy). A version stored by an older release loads with defaults for every field it lacks, and the journal says so once.
